classifications.decisive_evidence: Die changes are discrete consequences of submitted actions; no outcome-affecting state evolves while awaiting the next action.
The ball retains momentum in generated geometry. Recent motion predicts the delayed tilt, and a tilt that is useful now loses its advantage as the ball moves.
The bomb is solved through static, synchronous manipulation; no relevant action opportunity autonomously degrades.
Signature construction and reproduction advance through the agent's drag actions, not through autonomous task-state evolution between actions.

D1 is solvable by releasing its sole shaft at the fixed midpoint of the generated 34–42 tick window; its 30-degree tolerance covers every generated exact release tick. D2–D5 require visible phase-dependent choices whose timing advantage expires.
Every master/performance phase is fixed or derived from the agent's own recorded actions and clock; no recent visual window is required to schedule an expiring handoff.
Program state advances only when the agent steps the debugger; wiring remains static between submitted actions.
State transitions are consequences of discrete choices, with no relevant autonomous evolution between choices.
The recipe presentation supplies information for later static work; the information remains actionable and no concurrent action opportunity expires.
Held driving inputs persist while the vehicle and hazards move. Recent motion and geometry determine a delayed release or redirect, and the old control can become a collision.
Constellation revelation and target acquisition are driven by the submitted pointer/proxy actions; there is no autonomous expiring target state.

At D1–D2 the single echo stays entirely inside the lock radius around its known base coordinate, so motion observation is unnecessary. At D3–D5 recent visible motion predicts the delayed capture point and an old point can miss; Simplified only automates tracking after contact.

At Full D1 the fixed center remains inside the entire broad plate orbit, so tracking is unnecessary. Full D2–D5 require visible tracking and a stale pointer loses the hold. Simplified automatically tracks at every difficulty, leaving discrete route actions and agent-clock hold timing.
The autonomous domino run is not a concurrent control opportunity; the actionable reconstruction/diagnosis state is static.
The released marble keeps moving under live physics while post controls remain active. Recent velocity predicts the delayed correction, and the same correction loses value downstream.
Each board change is the synchronous result of an accepted swap; nothing relevant evolves while no action is supplied.
Terminal state changes only through submitted keystrokes and commands.
The desktop puzzle advances through discrete interface actions; no visible autonomous change makes a current action expire.
Assembly is action-driven, and controls are unavailable during the deterministic load animation; later certification can be scheduled from the load-start time.
Once movement starts, prisoner physics continues under held controls. Recent position and velocity in the generated projection determine a delayed release or jump, which can become too late.
The archive and gate state are changed through the agent's controls; no relevant action independently deteriorates between inputs.
A held movement action continues changing the camera and collision geometry. Recent views reveal the delayed release/redirect point, while continued motion can overshoot or fall.
The ritual is learned and performed through discrete interactions; waiting does not autonomously reduce the usefulness of the next correct action.
Bodies settle only after a submitted room rotation while further controls are blocked; there is no intervenable autonomous control mode.
Rod and view transformations are synchronous consequences of manipulation, with no autonomous action expiry.
Organisms keep moving with inertia and coupled responses while lure controls remain active. Recent trajectories determine the delayed lure coordinate, and an old coordinate loses influence.
The photographic target and event window move autonomously. Recent motion predicts the delayed shutter action, whose qualified capture opportunity closes.
The queued machine state advances synchronously when commands are issued; the agent's own action history determines the queue without a recent visual-motion requirement.
The visible tape/chart evidences the evolving price process. It predicts delayed order value, and the advantage of the same buy/sell action can disappear as prices move.
A submitted nudge starts coast, but controls are blocked until coast ends; afterward the placement state is static. Hold timing is available from the agent's own clock.
Held movement persists through generated geometry while scans fade. Recent motion and obstacles determine a delayed release/turn, and the old movement can collide or overshoot.
Swipe motion and duration are produced by the agent's own gesture, so the necessary timing is available from its action history rather than autonomous visible evolution.

At D1 and D2 a fixed seed-independent rack setting stays inside every moving-ring tolerance, so observation is unnecessary. At D3-D5 random moving poses exceed any fixed setting; recent ring motion predicts a correction whose value expires.
Every difficulty retains an autonomously moving packet interception subsystem with an active control in both interaction modes; recent motion predicts a capture opportunity that closes.
Voxel inspection and extraction progress through discrete pointer actions; the relevant spatial state is static between them.
The film presents information that is retained for later work; work controls are unavailable during playback and the later manipulation state is static.
Animation identifies the pieces, but the resulting placement actions remain valid indefinitely and are otherwise synchronous/static.
The target moves under live physics and cursor repulsion while pointer controls remain active. Recent target motion predicts the delayed click, and the old location loses its hit advantage.
Shell and cover geometry advances automatically. The recent sequence identifies the delayed inspection target, and its short inspection opportunity closes as the shell moves.
Impulses and coast are explicit discrete controls that advance a fixed simulation tick; state does not continue autonomously while the agent waits.

Food cooks continuously with generated target times while serve controls remain active. Visible cooking history predicts the delayed serve action, whose doneness advantage expires into under/overcooking.

Field decay and renewal are determined by the agent's own committed route times at every difficulty. The same route refresh remains effective later, so visible ant motion does not create a strictly expiring action.

A held movement input persists as the camera traverses generated room geometry. Recent movement/collisions determine a delayed release, turn, or capture, and continued motion can pass the useful point.
A fixed preview is followed by reproduction; it tests timing memory, but no controllable action opportunity expires during the preview.
Popup progression is governed by discrete dismissals; waiting does not make the same next correct dismissal less effective through relevant visible evolution.
Portal placement, parcel pushes, rotations, and transformed samples occur synchronously in action handlers.
Canonical nesting state changes only through submitted proxy moves; it is static between actions.

Every generated instance has a pre-run solution: place every object and set every depth before SETTLE, then let the complete force-settle phase finish without another outcome-affecting action. Its pre-run rate is 100%, above the 50% threshold.

Full mode requires continuous pointer tracking of the moving overload spark, and a stale pointer loses the hold. Simplified mode ignores spark position and reduces the interruption to a fixed hold timed from pointer-down.
The pulse and receiver move while contact/direction controls remain active. Recent relative motion predicts a delayed correction, and the old contact setting loses charge advantage.
Routing and switch state change only through submitted controls; there is no autonomous expiring action.
The relevant comparison and judgment state is static between selections.

classifications.public_name: Rorschach / Subjective Prompt With A Fixed Rubric
classifications.decisive_evidence: A fixed response cycle later re-enables controls and permanently archives its result; it creates information, not an expiring controllable opportunity.
Every gimbal and view change is synchronous with the agent's drag actions.
Full mode clicks moving on-screen keys, so recent motion predicts the delayed key location and an old click misses. Simplified mode uses stationary physical-key actions.
Probe duration is known from the agent's own hold clock, and successful probe eligibility persists after the visual response fades.
Lamp, shadow, and sample state change only in response to submitted controls.
Moving shards reveal phase/spatial information, but the later matching actions remain valid; synchronization holds are timed from the agent's own actions.
Lanes and hazards advance every tick independently of direction clicks. Recent motion predicts the delayed hop, while the same hop can become a collision or water failure.
The required physical-key action is the currently visible reel symbol. The generated token cycle changes autonomously, so an old key becomes wrong after the symbol switches.

At D1 a beam through the receiver's base remains within the 24-pixel tolerance over its entire 20–24-pixel motion, so tracking is unnecessary. At D2–D5 the motion exceeds tolerance; recent motion predicts an adjustment whose hit and charge advantage expires.
Parallax observation supports a later spatial solution, but the resulting selection/manipulation opportunity remains actionable rather than expiring.

Full mode exposes the lens during the one-shot live carrier field, where evidence opportunities move and expire. Simplified coordinate controls are usable in static review, whose evidence and later selection do not expire.

All coast is deterministically caused by the agent's own drag/release and can be braked from that action history; calendar clamping changes the later static state but creates no visually predicted expiring action.
Physics advances only through explicit coast/brake tick controls in this interaction mode, not autonomously while awaiting the next action.
Movement, turning, and firing are discrete step controls; the world does not keep evolving between actions.
Slice, probe, and extraction state changes only through the agent's controls.
Dice rolls and arithmetic progress through discrete submitted actions, with no expiring autonomous control opportunity.
Drift advances by submitted trace-sample index rather than task time; sonar fading removes visible information but does not reduce the effectiveness of a later sonar action.
The visible flight tail predicts the delayed catcher transform/arm action, and autonomous flight closes the catcher commit window.

D1-D2 use one pod and admit a successful constant fan assignment made before launch, so no in-flight observation or expiring correction is required. D3-D5 add a delayed second pod sharing fan spool and heat; successful control requires changing the fans during flight from recent pod and aperture motion.
The coordinate net must lead an autonomously moving/occluded target. Recent trajectory predicts the delayed aim, and the old aim loses its intercept opportunity.
The distorted visual content is static while the agent enters its answer.
Carrier phase drifts autonomously during the lock trial while sliders remain active. Recent waveform motion predicts a correction, and an old phase setting loses lock quality.
Cable physics is stepped synchronously after gripper movement or an explicit settle action; it does not evolve autonomously between actions.
